$comment: Integrations for the newsroom-agent-kit. Origin: Phase 2 discovery, extended in Phase 8 with Postiz self-hosted, the Postiz Agent Skill + CLI, HyperFrames and the now-required Node.js runtime. Read installAction per entry. 'none' means deliberately not installed and not connected. 'kit-managed-dependency' and 'planned' mean the kit provisions it as part of the reproducible setup. No entry is connected or authenticated without explicit user approval, and no credential is ever stored or printed by this project. The portable skill core remains fully useful without any of the optional entries.

policy.rationale: MCP servers and executable plugins are capability layers, not part of the portable skill core. Connecting an external account is never done implicitly.

integrations.name: Figma MCP server (official, remote)
integrations.valueForThisUser: Design-context extraction and design-to-code against a real design system; write-to-canvas in supported clients.
integrations.paidPlanEvidence: Access depends on plan and seat type. Starter seats get up to 20 tool calls per month. View/Collab seats on Organization or Enterprise get up to 6 per month. Dev/Full seats get up to 200/day on Professional and up to 600/day on Enterprise. See https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/rate-limits-access/
integrations.clientSupportNote: Figma states that only clients listed in the Figma MCP Catalog can connect, and that new clients must join a waitlist. Whether the installed OpenCode 2.0.22 and Cline 0.0.43 are catalog-listed is NOT verified. Treat as likely blocked until confirmed at https://www.figma.com/mcp-catalog/.
integrations.additionalNote: Figma also publishes its own skills for MCP clients. Those would be agent-specific and must not be added to the canonical .agents core.

integrations.name: Canva MCP server (official, remote)
integrations.valueForThisUser: Design generation and editing, brand kits and asset management, multi-format export, and commenting for social asset production.
integrations.paidPlanEvidence: Not established from the documentation reviewed.
integrations.authMethod: Canva Developer Platform app plus per-user OAuth
integrations.clientSupportNote: The published documentation is written for IT admins and for teams embedding Canva into their own assistants, not for an individual connecting a personal coding agent. Individual setup is documented separately in the Canva Help Center.

integrations.name: Cline plugin: agent-browser
integrations.valueForThisUser: Browser automation for checking live pages and publishing output.
integrations.risk: Executable TypeScript plugin that runs inside Cline. Not portable and not part of the agent-agnostic core.

integrations.name: Cline plugin: jev-browser
integrations.valueForThisUser: Browser control with recording overlay and model-driven navigation.
integrations.risk: Highest-risk item reviewed. Executable TypeScript with dedicated credentials.ts, credentials.test.ts, a bundled remote-helper binary per platform, and IPC. It stores and manages external service credentials. Do not install without a dedicated review.

integrations.name: AccessLint MCP server
integrations.valueForThisUser: Would power the accesslint accessibility-audit, accessibility-scan and accessibility-inspect skills.
integrations.reasonNotSelected: Every accesslint skill declares AccessLint MCP tools in allowed-tools, so the skills are inert without this server. The repository also has no LICENSE file. The core already covers WCAG guidance through the instruction-only accessibility-compliance skill.

integrations.name: ScrapeCreators REST API
integrations.valueForThisUser: Cross-platform social scraping: profiles, posts, comments, transcripts, ads, trends and engagement metrics.
integrations.riskNote: The public-post research skills in that repository are declared as requiring this key, so the whole family is gated behind a paid service. It also carries a scraping/ToS dimension the user should consider before use.

integrations.name: Impeccable CLI and design-detector hook
integrations.valueForThisUser: Deterministic anti-pattern detection after UI edits, live browser iteration, and project context loading.
integrations.requiresRuntime: self-contained launcher; upstream states no Node or other runtime is required
integrations.riskNote: No prebuilt binary is committed at the pinned ref. The launcher downloads a binary on first run, which means remote code execution at install time and on every upgrade. The skill degrades gracefully if the launcher is unavailable.
integrations.decision: The portable instruction layer is installed as core; the CLI, hooks and live-browser layer stay out of the default install.

integrations.name: GitHub CLI (gh)
integrations.installPlan: ALREADY PRESENT. No action needed and the kit does not manage it. Verified with "gh --version" and "gh auth status"; no credential value was read or recorded.
integrations.phase8DiscoveryNote: HISTORICAL. During Phase 2 discovery gh was absent and recorded as "required-later-not-installed", to be used only for publishing in Phase 6. Phase 6 installed and authorised it. It is not a dependency of the kit: nothing in the install, update, verify or uninstall path calls it.
integrations.valueForThisUser: NOT a dependency of this kit. Nothing in the install, update, verify or uninstall path calls gh. It was used once, in Phase 6, to create and publish this repository, and is recorded here only because it is present on the machine and owned by the user, not by the kit.

integrations.name: Node.js / npm
integrations.changeReason: Node moved from an explicitly avoided optional prerequisite to a required managed runtime when the Postiz and HyperFrames extensions were added.
integrations.phase8bNote: Kept as the Phase 8 discovery record: at that point Node was absent and recorded as an avoided optional prerequisite. It became required when the Zernio and HyperFrames extensions were added, then was actually installed in Phase 9.
integrations.phase8Note: HISTORICAL. At Phase 8 discovery Node was recorded as absent and as an avoided optional prerequisite, on the basis that the instruction-only core needed no runtime. It became required when execution backends were added. The original justification cited the HyperFrames CLI and the Postiz CLI; Postiz was evaluated and not selected in Phase 8B, so the current justification is HyperFrames plus Zernio.
integrations.valueForThisUser: REQUIRED. One Node.js LTS runtime serves both selected CLIs: the hyperframes npm package, which declares engines.node >=22, and @zernio/cli, which declares no engines field but whose own CI builds on Node 24. Node 24 satisfies both.
integrations.installPlan: PROVISIONED. winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS -e --scope user, only when a compatible Node is not already detected. Ownership is "shared": a normal kit uninstall must NOT remove Node, because global npm CLIs and user scripts depend on it. See manifest/dependencies.json.

integrations.name: Postiz self-hosted (local compose stack)
integrations.phase8bOutcome: REJECTED as the default backend in Phase 8B. Preserved as the record of an evaluated alternative. Do NOT provision WSL2, Docker Desktop or the Postiz stack as part of the default setup.
integrations.rejectionReason: BLOCK-RAM: this machine has 3.44 GB total RAM with 0.24 GB free, against a nine-container stack needing roughly 2.3-3 GB plus 1-1.5 GB of runtime. BLOCK-WSL: WSL is not installed and installing it needs elevation plus a reboot. Neither is automatable, and neither improves over time.
integrations.valueForThisUser: The operational execution layer for social publishing: post, schedule, draft, queue, cross-post, upload media, discover integrations, read post and platform analytics.
integrations.architecture: Coding Agent -> Postiz Agent Skill / CLI -> local self-hosted Postiz -> social platform APIs
integrations.authMethod: API key issued by the LOCAL instance, with POSTIZ_API_URL=http://localhost:4007
integrations.rejectedAuthMethod: postiz auth:login OAuth2 device flow. Evidence: postiz-agent/src/auth.ts:9 DEFAULT_AUTH_SERVER = 'https://cli-auth.postiz.com'. It depends on Postiz-hosted infrastructure, which this architecture forbids.
integrations.mcpNote: No MCP layer is proposed. The Skill plus CLI path reaches every capability found, needs no hosted endpoint and no agent-specific registration. No MCP will be added without user approval and a documented missing capability.
integrations.humanOnlyStep: The user generates the API key in their own local Postiz instance under Settings > API Keys and enters it into the local environment. The agent never handles that secret.
integrations.installPlan: NOT PROVISIONED. Superseded by zernio in Phase 8B. Would require Docker Desktop on WSL2, both currently absent, on hardware that cannot host the stack.
integrations.persistentData: Six named Docker volumes. Never removed by a normal uninstall; no 'down -v', no 'volume rm', no prune.
integrations.executableCodeSurface: Nine continuously running containers executing AGPL-3.0 code, holding social platform tokens and user content.

integrations.name: Postiz Agent Skill + CLI (npm: postiz)
integrations.phase8bOutcome: REJECTED as the default backend in Phase 8B, together with the self-hosted stack it depends on. Not installed.
integrations.valueForThisUser: The agent-facing execution surface for the self-hosted Postiz instance.
integrations.skill: postiz (single portable SKILL.md, ~31 KB, declares required env POSTIZ_API_URL)
integrations.installPlan: NOT PROVISIONED. Superseded by zernio in Phase 8B.
integrations.executableCodeSurface: npm package executed by the agent on every publishing operation.

integrations.name: Zernio (SaaS social execution backend)
integrations.phase8bOutcome: SELECTED in Phase 8B as the social execution backend, replacing Postiz self-hosted.
integrations.selectionReason: Runs on this machine with no local services, no WSL, no Docker and no elevation. Materially stronger at the community work this user actually does: inbox/DMs, comment replies, reviews, broadcasts, drip sequences and comment-to-DM automations. Cleaner agent integration with JSON on stdout and prompts on stderr. Scoped read-only API keys. Pre-flight post validation. Verifiable end-to-end at zero cost on the free 2-account tier.
integrations.license: MIT for the client, CLI and skills. The service is proprietary SaaS on Vercel.
integrations.architecture: Coding Agent -> zernio skill -> @zernio/cli -> Zernio REST API -> social platform APIs
integrations.freeTier: First 2 connected social accounts free, no credit card required.
integrations.authMethod: zernio auth:login device authorization flow. The CLI opens a browser and creates the key automatically, so the user never handles a secret.
integrations.credentialStorage: %USERPROFILE%\.zernio\config.json, overridable by environment variable. No chmod is applied, so treat it as a secret on Windows.
integrations.dataControl: Content, DMs, comments and social OAuth tokens live on Zernio's infrastructure, not on the user's machine. Any account can be disconnected at any time.
integrations.executableCodeSurface: MIT npm CLI. Verified: it never writes to .claude, .agents, .cursor, .codex or .gemini, and carries no telemetry.
integrations.expectedMonthlyCost: $0/month. The intended scope is the first 2 connected accounts on the free tier; every other platform stays manual.
integrations.costNotDeterministic: Total cost depends on which accounts the installer connects, which is their decision. This kit does not choose and does not require any particular account.
integrations.conditionalExampleOnly: CONDITIONAL ARITHMETIC EXAMPLE, NOT the expected cost. If someone connected all 8 platforms of a typical media outlet, that would be 8 accounts = 2 free + 6 x $6 = $36/month. The intended setup here uses the 2 free accounts and costs $0.
integrations.passThroughCosts: The free tier covers connected ACCOUNTS, not every platform API charge. X is passed through at X exact rates with zero markup: reads $0.005, post and DM sends $0.015, posts containing a URL $0.200. X analytics and inbox sync are opt-in and stay off. Messages sent are free to 10,000/month. If neither connected account is on X, the ongoing cost is $0.

integrations.name: Zernio Agent Skills + CLI (npm: @zernio/cli)
integrations.packageNameCaveat: The unscoped npm package 'zernio' does not exist, so 'npx zernio' fails. Install the scoped @zernio/cli. The legacy 'late' bin name collides with an unrelated unscoped npm package.
integrations.engines: none declared; the project's own CI builds and publishes on Node 24
integrations.commandSurface: 19 hand-written command groups plus 112 commands auto-generated from the OpenAPI spec
integrations.skillsNote: zernio ships inside the npm package and covers CLI operations. zernio-api is a separate REST reference with 24 progressive-disclosure rule files, covering blogs, voice, phone numbers, per-platform constraints and webhooks that the CLI does not state.
integrations.skillsDeferred: Six single-purpose skills from the official Agent Skills index (schedule-post, connect-account, list-analytics, send-message, run-ads, manage-blog-articles) are not installed by default. They duplicate the CLI skill through raw REST. Each is sha256-pinned in manifest/dependencies.json if a gap ever appears.
integrations.installPlan: npm install -g @zernio/cli, performed by the installer once the shared Node.js runtime is present. Ownership is 'kit-installed'.
integrations.executableCodeSurface: npm package invoked per command. No background service, no ports, no local database.

integrations.name: Zernio MCP server (hosted)
integrations.valueForThisUser: None by default. The CLI already exposes the whole operational surface.
integrations.installPlan: Do not install. It would add a hosted endpoint, a second authentication model and extra tool definitions for no capability gain. Only reconsider if a concrete capability gap appears in the CLI, and only with explicit user approval.

integrations.name: HyperFrames (deterministic code-driven motion graphics and video)
integrations.valueForThisUser: Deterministic, code-driven motion graphics and video rendered locally: kinetic typography, animated stats, lower thirds, headline cards, overlays, animated screenshots, explainer visuals and reusable media templates.
integrations.architecture: Coding Agent -> global HyperFrames Agent Skills -> HyperFrames CLI/runtime -> local deterministic render
integrations.cloudNote: The upstream aws-lambda and gcp-cloud-run packages and examples exist but are NOT part of this architecture. They stay unconfigured and are documented as optional.
integrations.generativeNote: Image-generation and video-generation models are out of scope. Within media-use, local media handling, composition, audio and icons are core; generative image, music and voice calls are optional and unconfigured.
rejectedUpstreamCommands: npx hyperframes skills (bare - installs the full published set)
integrations.executableCodeSurface: Node CLI, a puppeteer-managed headless browser, FFmpeg encoding, and esbuild/fontkit processing.
integrations.skillNamedHyperframesCli: "hyperframes-cli" is a skill id, not the npm package name.
integrations.executableSkillContent: 5 of the 10 core skills contain 77 reviewed and allowlisted scripts. See docs/security.md SEC-15.
integrations.installPlan: PROVISIONED. Node.js and FFmpeg via winget at user scope, then npm install -g hyperframes@0.8.126, then the 10 core skills materialised into %USERPROFILE%\.agents\skills. Node.js and FFmpeg are ownership shared and are never removed by a normal uninstall.
integrations.cliPackageNote: The published npm package is the unscoped name "hyperframes". "@hyperframes/cli" is the monorepo-internal name and is not on the registry. Verified against the registry on 2026-10-05.
integrations.skillInstallRationale: The 10 core skills are declared in manifest/skills.json as PINNED FETCH entries and materialised reproducibly from the reviewed upstream ref dc3665ab into canonical %USERPROFILE%\.agents\skills by the normal installer. They are NOT hand-maintained vendored forks under vendor/skills/, and they are not modified. Upstream's own skill installer was rejected because it writes ~/.claude/skills and symlinks into other agents' directories, both of which this project forbids. In this project a "vendored" entry specifically means a fork whose upstream product claims were rewritten (SEC-07); that does not apply to a tool the kit actually installs, so no fork was created.
integrations.vendoredSkillsUnaffected: The 27 real vendored forks under vendor/skills/ are unchanged and remain a separate delivery mode.

upstreamCommandAssessment.method: Static source inspection of packages/cli/src/commands/skills.ts and init.ts at the reviewed ref. No upstream command was executed to test this.

readOnly.why: checkCommand performs no filesystem writes. Read-only freshness report, also available as --json for CI.

writesVendorDirectory.why: updateSkills writes real files to ~/.claude/skills, which Claude Code reads at global priority, in addition to ~/.agents/skills, then mirrorGlobalSkills fans them into other agents' directories. Violates the .agents-only rule and the no-symlink constraint.

init.ts keepSkillsCurrent documents that the install "lands once GLOBALLY (~/.claude/skills + ~/.agents/skills)". init calls it, so scaffolding a project also refreshes global skills into a vendor directory.

rejected.why: The parent handler runs updateSkills({ all: true }) when no positional is given, installing the FULL published set.

upstreamCommandAssessment.kitPolicy: This kit installs and refreshes HyperFrames skills ONLY through manifest/skills.json and the installer, which writes solely to %USERPROFILE%\.agents\skills. No upstream skill-lifecycle command is used for global skill installation or updates, at any time.

notEvaluated.item: Google Docs / Sheets / Canva-adjacent CMS MCP servers
notEvaluated.reason: Out of scope for a community manager and newsroom workflow unless the user names a specific tool.
No skill in this area was selected, so no integration was researched.

stateSchema: status and installAction describe the CURRENT state. Fields named phase, phase8bOutcome, changedInPhase or *Note describe history and are not overwritten.
costSchema: expectedMonthlyCost is the cost of the intended setup. conditionalExampleOnly is illustrative arithmetic for a different account count and must never be read as the expected cost. passThroughCosts lists charges that survive the free tier.
